stories.h2: The drone was only the beginning.
stories.lead: “You can automate the flying of drones from Point A to Point B,” says Ankit Mishra, “but if at Point B the battery dies, then someone has to be there to recharge it.” His company, AlgoFET, solved what sat around the drone: charging docks, precision landing, self-charging batteries and a backup for every critical step.
stories.sub: Ankit joined ARTPARK as an engineer working on battery management. Today he is a founder. The story usually told is about flight. The more useful one is about the system that lets a drone fly again, at any hour, with no one on the ground.

stories.caption: AlgoFET’s AlgoPAD charging dock, Bengaluru

stories.h2: From a laser link to a company built in India.
stories.lead: QOSMIC’s founders set out to build a quantum satellite. Customers told them what they actually needed: a faster way to bring satellite data down to Earth. Turning that into a company meant an optical ground station, a space-grade steering mirror, qualification tests and a seed round, each a different kind of work around the same science.
stories.sub: “A decade ago, a company like this would have had to be built in the US or Europe,” says co-founder and CEO Shreyaans Jain. What it takes for research capability to become an enterprise.
stories.imageAlt: Prof. Aloke Kumar, co-founder of QOSMIC, speaking at a seminar
stories.caption: Prof. Aloke Kumar, QOSMIC co-founder
sources: ARTPARK and QOSMIC LinkedIn posts on the Fast Steering Mirror qualification
metric: seed round led by Accel and Prosus, with South Park Commons and ARTPARK

stories.h2: Vaani became much more than a speech dataset.
stories.lead: Most speech technology was not built for the way India actually talks. Project Vaani, by IISc and ARTPARK and funded by Google, is recording it district by district and opening it to everyone: more than 31,000 hours of speech from over 1.5 lakh people, in 105 languages.
stories.sub: How public research becomes a platform that others build on, from the first publicly available Garo speech-to-text model in Shillong to Hindi call-centre analytics.

rail.text: I always wanted to build a startup. Even during college, I had ideas, but I never had a de-risked environment.

rail.pull: That’s not a people problem; it’s a systems problem.
This is like the wireless equivalent of fibre optic.

rail.match: We were not born to fly
